title: Adopt Popup-Mediated Local Clearance Policy
summary: Resolve the FP-MCP-235 reconciliation by explicitly adopting popup-mediated local clearance for ForgePilot MCP guarded starts. This decision supersedes the FP-MCP-217 prohibition on MCP-created local clearance for this scoped use case. The reason is operational: the operator is mostly on mobile, approvals are time-limited, and requiring a separately pasted local Python/script command made the clearance window brittle and error-prone. The adopted posture is not equivalent to hands-on-keyboard outside-MCP clearance; it is a deliberate weaker but accepted posture with explicit compensating controls. The forgepilot_create_operator_local_execution_clearance tool may create one exact, short-lived, single-use local clearance only after explicit ChatGPT/MCP popup approval and validation of committed approval evidence, current target HEAD, branch, clean workspace, request artifact, execution-base ancestry, gitignored clearance path, model, run mode, request id, and target workspace. This packet records policy only and does not create clearance, consume approval, contact runner start, start OpenCode, or run FP-027.
caveats: This is a deliberate revision of FP-MCP-217, not a UX-only restatement.
A ChatGPT/MCP popup remains inside the model-callable tool surface; the operator approves a model-proposed action rather than independently initiating the clearance outside MCP.
The successful FP-MCP-233 run is not used as proof that the policy was already clean; it remains historically governance-incomplete until FP-MCP-237 records its integrity review.
This policy adoption does not retroactively mark the FP-MCP-233 approval consumed.
The approval-consumption fix must still be activated and verified in a later packet.
Popup-mediated clearance is permitted only through the exact scoped tool contract; any broad, wildcard, standing, or long-lived clearance remains forbidden.

supersedes.previousRule: MCP may observe and validate operator-local clearance but must not create it; clearance creation is a hands-on-keyboard act outside the model-callable MCP surface.
supersedes.supersededForScope: ForgePilot MCP guarded starts using the exact popup-mediated clearance creation tool contract.

adoptedRule.rule: MCP may create one local execution-clearance.json artifact only after explicit ChatGPT/MCP popup approval and only for the exact validated tuple supplied to the tool.
adoptedRule.scope: Guarded ForgePilot MCP remote-runner starts; initially DESIGN_ONLY/dev canary style starts unless a later packet broadens or restricts the policy.
notAllowed: creation without committed valid approval evidence
creation when target workspace is dirty
creation when current HEAD does not equal requestArtifactCommit
creation when executionBaseCommit is not ancestor of requestArtifactCommit

rationale.timingConstraint: structured approvals and clearances expire quickly
rationale.uxProblem: manual shell/Python clearance creation consumed the approval window and increased operator error risk
rationale.acceptedTradeoff: weaker than outside-MCP hands-on-keyboard clearance but operationally usable with strong tuple and state gates

threatModelRevision.oldThreatControl: model-callable MCP surface could not create final clearance artifact
threatModelRevision.newThreatControl: model can propose a clearance-writing call, but the user must approve the popup and the tool validates exact committed approval and live workspace state before writing
threatModelRevision.residualRisk: user may approve model-proposed clearance creation inside ChatGPT without an independent out-of-band local action

compensatingControls: approval must be valid, unexpired, unconsumed, unrevoked, and unquarantined
current target branch and HEAD must match
request artifact must exist and bind to execution base
executionBaseCommit must be ancestor of requestArtifactCommit
tool does not clear disable switch
tool does not contact runner start endpoint
